title: Adaptive communication gating for multi-agent workflows
research_question: Can a MAPE-K-inspired controller that dynamically adjusts inter-agent communication frequency and routing improve task success per token and latency in multi-agent LLM workflows compared with fixed communication patterns?
hypothesis: In multi-agent workflows, many failures and inefficiencies come from static communication policies rather than weak individual agents; an adaptive controller that monitors collaboration signals and selectively triggers, suppresses, or reroutes messages will improve efficiency and maintain or increase solution quality.
motivation: The knowledge base shows a rejected idea around Bayesian uncertainty-aware scheduling for multi-agent workflows, suggesting scheduling-only uncertainty handling may be too close to existing directions or insufficiently novel. Separately, the self-adaptive systems literature in the KB highlights an open gap: uncertainty handling is commonly added to analyze/plan loops, but future work calls for extension to additional domains and heterogeneous requirements. A promising unexplored angle is to transfer self-adaptive MAPE-K control into agentic workflow optimization, not for task scheduling itself, but for communication management under runtime uncertainty. Multi-agent LLM systems often overspend tokens through unnecessary discussion or fail because useful agents are not consulted at the right time. Adaptive communication gating directly targets this bottleneck and offers a clearer novelty boundary than another scheduler proposal.
